title: DualSlide
shortDescription: Present two synchronized PowerPoint decks on separate displays.
description:
Present together with DualSlide. Show two matching PowerPoint presentations on separate displays while controlling the presenter deck normally. The audience deck follows slides, ordinary animation steps, and pointer movements.

Useful for translated presentations, parallel-language talks, and audience-specific versions of the same presentation. PowerPoint renders both decks natively, including animations.

Keep both shows on the last slide and move backward or forward without restarting. Press Escape to exit. Original files open read-only and are not saved by DualSlide.

REQUIRES: Windows 11 x64, the Microsoft PowerPoint desktop application installed separately, two displays in Extend mode, and presentations with matching slide counts, aspect ratios, and ordinary animation sequences. PowerPoint for the web is not supported. Microsoft PowerPoint is not included.

Synchronization is not frame-locked. Shape-specific animation triggers, ink mirroring, and synchronized audio/video clocks are outside scope. The audience laser is a PowerPoint-style approximation; custom laser colors are not mirrored.

An independent utility by Silviu Vlasceanu. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.
features: Synchronize slides and ordinary animation steps
Mirror native cursor artwork and a red laser-style pointer
Separate display selection and mixed-DPI support
Keep the final slide visible until Escape
certificationNotes: Requires Microsoft PowerPoint desktop (not bundled) and two extended displays. Select two .pptx decks with identical slide counts, aspect ratios, and ordinary animation sequences, assign separate displays, then Start. Navigate the presenter deck with arrows, clicks or wheel. Final slide stays visible; Escape exits both shows. No login required. runFullTrust is required for WinForms/WPF, PowerPoint COM automation, cross-display Win32 window positioning, and slideshow-scoped keyboard/mouse hooks. The app does not require administrator rights, install services/drivers, upload presentations, or record keystroke history. Original files open read-only and are never saved.
